analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: it adds docs/reports/2026-10-21-mixed-step-prefill-geometry.md (head lines 1-144) and one index link in docs/reports/README.md (line 7). It changes no provider code, defaults, key handling, attestation, WebSocket contract, cache storage or authorization logic, so no trust boundary, asset or mitigation in the threat model is altered.

Security-relevant content in the report: (1) It records that the 2,048/4,096 prefill chunk and step-token geometry raises p99 and max inter-token gaps 2-3x, and drops per-stream decode to 1.5-2.6 tok/s under 32k prompts. This is a performance and availability characteristic (T-010/T-029 neighborhood). It is documented with limitations and does not itself introduce a vulnerability. (2) KV-subtracted activation peaks rise 0.1-1.3 GiB. GPT-OSS peaks 0.1 GiB above its 3.5 GiB floor, and Qwen3.5-9B sits above its 5.5 GiB floor. These are memory-admission floors, and the report states they need long-context re-measurement. This is a possible OOM or DoS concern for the code change that the report backs, but that code change is not in this PR's supplied units. The report states it is not quality qualification. (3) The load test used unique nonces with no prefix reuse, so it does not touch the T-041 cache/TTFT oracle. It states that dense Qwen donors now leave recurrent checkpoints every 2,048 tokens, which is a behavior change in the unseen code, not in this PR. (4) The Gemma media ceiling of 512 is described as protecting against a 1.84 GiB score-tensor growth. This is a mitigation described in prose only.

The report links to ../architecture/inference.md#prompt-geometry, which is not supplied. Whether the corresponding code and defaults, including the activation-floor constants, are safe cannot be verified from this batch. The README change adds a relative link only. No secrets, credentials or sensitive data appear in the added text. No findings.
